name: Illinois
source: Illinois Department of Revenue income tax rates page (4.95% of net income since 2017-07-01, read 2026-10-22) and exemption allowance answer 851 (2,850 for 2025, indexed); 2026 exemption 2,925 from the Tax Foundation 2026 table; Illinois Attorney General 2023 estate tax fact sheet (read 2026-10-22)

state_base.note: Illinois starts from federal adjusted (or taxable) income and keeps the federal treatment of 401(k) deferrals, Traditional IRA deposits and HSA deposits (no add-back; only California and New Jersey tax HSA deposits). Not checked against a state ruling.

exemptions.note: Exemption allowance 2,925 per person and dependent for 2026 (2,850 for 2025 from IDOR; 2026 from Tax Foundation), plus 1,000 per taxpayer or spouse 65 or older (IDOR). Not modelled: no exemption at all above federal AGI 250,000 (500,000 joint).

retirement_exclusion.note: Illinois subtracts all federally taxed distributions from qualified employer plans and IRAs (and Social Security) at any age (IL-1040 line 5; state-costs.csv retirement_income and Kiplinger agree, confirmed primary: https://tax.illinois.gov/individuals/pension.html, validation run 2, 2026-10-22).

estate_inheritance.note: Illinois estate tax: 4,000,000 exclusion (a threshold, not a credit; unchanged for 2026 per Faegre Drinker and SB 2038 text), no portability. The tax is the interrelated computation of the Attorney General: the smaller of the old federal state death tax credit table on (taxable estate - 60,000) and 40% of the taxable estate above 4,000,000, where the taxable estate is the estate less the Illinois tax itself. The brackets here are that result solved on the estate above 4,000,000 (28.57% to 5,359,167, then r/(1+r) of each credit-table rate) and reproduce the fact sheet's examples: 4,000,000 owes 0 and 5,000,000 owes 285,714 (primary, read 2026-10-22). Not modelled: deductions other than the tax itself, apportionment for property outside Illinois.

social_security.note: Illinois does not tax Social Security benefits; it is not among the states that tax them in Kiplinger 2026 (https://www.kiplinger.com/taxes/states-that-tax-social-security-benefits) and state-costs.csv column ss_taxed. Confirmed primary on https://tax.illinois.gov/individuals/pension.html (validation run 2, 2026-10-22).

local_income_tax.check_at: Tax Foundation local income taxes primer
local_income_tax.note: Illinois cities and counties levy no income tax (Tax Foundation local income tax list and state-costs.csv local_income_tax agree).

sales_tax.check_at: Illinois revenue department sales and use tax rate tables
sales_tax.source: Tax Foundation, State and Local Sales Tax Rates, Midyear 2026 (https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/2026-sales-tax-rates-midyear/), as of 2026-07-01; groceries and clothing: https://tax.illinois.gov/research/publications/bulletins/fy-2026-11.html and https://zamp.com/blog/sales-tax-on-clothing
sales_tax.note: Rates as fractions; avg_local_rate is the combined less the state rate, at least 0. vehicle_rate is the purchase tax on a car: assumed equal to the combined rate. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py. Groceries and clothing: grocery_rate is the state rate on groceries (0.0) plus the average local rate where locals tax them (locals: partly); research note: State 1% grocery tax repealed 2026-01-01 (PA 103-0781); ~656 municipalities and 3 counties adopted 1% local grocery tax; RTA/MED food taxes remain; estimate 1% local + ~0.25% avg RTA/MED instead of general local avg. clothing_taxable is true (research: yes; taxed). Set by hand from .claude/state/research/grocery-tax.csv and clothing-tax.csv (s329).

property_tax.check_at: Census ACS 2024 1-year tables B25090 and B25082 at https://data.census.gov
property_tax.source: Census ACS 2024 1-year (B25090 / B25082) as compiled at https://floridaprobateandfamilylaw.com/blog/effective-property-tax-rates-by-state-2025/
property_tax.note: Effective rate: real-estate taxes paid divided by home value, owner-occupied homes. Senior relief, homestead caps and freezes are not in it (a buyer pays the full rate). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

home_insurance.source: Insurify state table for a 300,000 dwelling (https://insurify.com/homeowners-insurance/states/), October 2026
home_insurance.note: Average annual premium for a 300,000 dwelling. Quote averages differ by 20 to 40 percent between publishers, so the model uses it as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_insurance.source: Insurify full coverage, monthly times 12 (https://insurify.com/car-insurance/states/), October 2026
car_insurance.note: Average annual full-coverage premium. Used as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_taxes.source: Illinois Secretary of State standard passenger registration fee of 151 a year, as quoted by several fee guides (s292 search, 2026-10-22) and state-costs.csv column vehicle_tax
car_taxes.note: Flat annual passenger-car registration of 151; Illinois has no annual vehicle property tax. The primary fee page could not be fetched and the guides quoting it are weak, so unconfirmed. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py; average_annual set by hand in s292 (rerunning the importer resets it to 0). Confirmed primary on https://www.ilga.gov/Documents/legislation/ilcs/documents/062500050K3-806.htm (validation run 2, 2026-10-22).

fuel.source: Excise: https://tax.illinois.gov/research/publications/bulletins/fy-2026-23.html (validation run 2, 2026-10-22); price: USGasGauge state-by-year table (AAA data), 2024 annual average
fuel.note: gas_tax_per_gallon is the state excise in dollars, without sales tax on fuel: 0.483 for all of 2026 (P.A. 104-0468 suspended the July 2026 increase); average_price_per_gallon is the 2024 average pump price (grade unclear, about regular). Set by hand from the primary source in validation run 2, 2026-10-22; importStateCosts.py keeps a hand-set section.

utilities.source: EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.B, residential price, January to July 2026
utilities.note: Average residential electricity price in dollars per kWh, January to July 2026 (a partial year). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

housing.check_at: https://fred.stlouisfed.org (Zillow Home Value Index by state) and https://meric.mo.gov/data/cost-living-data-series
housing.source: Zillow Home Value Index by state via FRED (September 2026); MERIC Cost of Living Data Series housing index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026
housing.note: typical_home_value is the Zillow Home Value Index (all homes, middle tier); cost_index is the MERIC housing cost index (US = 100), used to scale rent after a move. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

health_premiums.check_at: https://www.kff.org/affordable-care-act/state-indicator/average-marketplace-premiums-by-metal-tier/, Illinois insurance department Medigap rate guide and the CMS MA Landscape and Part D files (https://www.cms.gov)
health_premiums.source: KFF Average Marketplace Premiums by Metal Tier 2026 (benchmark silver at 40, times the federal age curve 2.124 for 60); MoneyGeek Medicare Supplement Plan G at 65, 2026; KFF Average Monthly Premium for PDPs, 2024; MedicareSupplement.com analysis of the CMS 2026 MA Landscape files
health_premiums.note: Monthly premiums per person, unsubsidized list prices: aca_60_monthly is the benchmark silver plan at 60 (estimated from the age-40 figure), medigap_g_monthly Plan G at 65, part_d_monthly the enrollment-weighted Part D plan, medicare_advantage_monthly the average Medicare Advantage premium. Null means no usable figure; a move then leaves that premium unchanged. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

price_indexes.source: MERIC Cost of Living Data Series grocery index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026; BEA Regional Price Parities by state, goods and other services (US = 100), 2024, release of 2026-02-19 via FRED
price_indexes.note: Price levels with US = 100: grocery_index is the MERIC grocery index, bea_goods and bea_services the BEA Regional Price Parities for goods and for services other than rent. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

long_term_care.source: Genworth / CareScout Cost of Care Survey 2024, Ranked State Data Tables, state medians (https://assets.carescout.com/a41bb6478c/298701.pdf)
long_term_care.note: State median monthly costs: a home health aide, an assisted living facility and a private nursing home room. Stored for reference; the model does not use them. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.
